My land here in Quzhou is about 7 mu total — the same plots my family has worked for decades. I am getting old, my back is not what it was, so I have to be practical about what I take on.

I will grow winter wheat on 6 mu, the same as always. My son-in-law helps me hire the rotary tiller from the village service station in October. I will use the improved wheat variety the township agricultural office promoted last year — my neighbor Old Zhang used it and got a decent harvest. I always put down compound fertilizer at planting and urea again at jointing in spring. That is what my father did, and I have done it for 40 years. I will irrigate at sowing, before winter sets in, at green-up, and once more at grain filling — four times. I will hire someone to spray for aphids and wheat rust in spring, two times usually.

After wheat harvest in June, I will plant summer maize on the same 6 mu — no tillage, just direct seeding into the stubble. The seed dealer in town sells Zhengdan 958, that is what most people around here use. I will put fertilizer on twice. If July rains are poor I will pump once or twice from the well.

On my remaining 1 mu near the house, I will plant sweet potato in spring. That is for the family to eat and to give to grandchildren. I do this by hand myself.
